responsibility: This module is GCC’s language-specific frontend for Go, covering the full source-language pipeline from reading Go source through package import/export and lowering into backend-neutral IR for code generation. Its main file groups define the Go compiler’s core representations and passes: lexical analysis and recursive-descent parsing (`lex*`, `parse*`) build the package-wide `Gogo` IR (`gogo*`, `go.cc`); expression, statement, and type subsystems (`expressions*`, `statements*`, `types*`, plus `operator.h`) implement Go semantics such as constant evaluation, declarations, control flow, method/type rules, and backend type conversion; import/export and archive support (`import*`, `import-archive.cc`, `export*`) serialize and reconstruct package metadata and inlineable bodies across compilations; analysis and lowering passes such as escape analysis and write-barrier insertion (`escape*`, `wb.cc`) adapt Go semantics to runtime and GC requirements; runtime, unsafe, embed, and naming support (`runtime*`, `unsafe.cc`, `embed.cc`, `names.cc`, `go-encode-id*`) connect frontend constructs to libgo/runtime helpers, symbol mangling, and special builtins; and shared diagnostics, source locations, dumps, and frontend optimization/debug controls (`go-diagnostics*`, `go-linemap.h`, `ast-dump*`, `go-dump*`, `go-optimize*`) provide reporting and developer-facing instrumentation. Overall, this module is responsible for understanding Go language rules and package format, performing Go-specific analyses and transformations, and translating Go programs into the backend interface defined by `backend.h`.
